title: Weight Transfer Wrist Shot
description: Learn how to properly transfer your weight from back foot to front foot on a wrist shot. This drill breaks down the kinetic chain — from your feet through your hips and core into your release.
dos: Start with weight on your back foot
Step into the puck as you release
Point your toe where you want the puck to go
Keep your hands away from your body
Follow through — blade should point at target
donts: Keep your weight centered — you'll lose power
Open your shoulders before the puck leaves
Look up before finishing your release
Cradle the puck too long — get it off quick

title: Foundation Stickhandling
description: Stationary stickhandling drill to build soft hands and puck feel. Focuses on top-hand control, wrist flexion, and keeping your head up.
dos: Keep your top hand loose — it controls the blade
Cup the puck with the blade
Keep your eyes up, feel the puck
Use your wrist, not your whole arm
donts: Death grip the stick — choke it and you lose feel
Slap at the puck — smooth controlled touches
keyCues: Feel it, don't look at it

title: Toe Drag Release
description: Toe drag to release into a powerful shot. Build up to it.
whatYouNeed: A cone (or puck, bucket, chair with a stick)
dos: Hips rotate toward net, feet stay mostly planted
Start easy, feet not too close to the cone
Drag the puck with the toe, get a powerful pop off release
Elbow up, allow the sling push-pull motion
As you improve, move your feet closer to the cone — release the puck between your feet with weight on top of the puck for flex and power
donts: Don't step away from the cone before the release
Don't look down at the puck the whole time

title: Explosive Pop Snap
description: Train a quicker, more explosive snap that transfers to every shot type.
whatYouNeed: Two broken sticks, 1-3 feet gap between them
dos: Focus solely on the snap
Keep your body relaxed
Pop the puck from the toe of the blade as quick as you can
donts: Don't drag the puck and turn it into a Bedard style shot
You should solely be focusing on the snap release
Don't need to move your feet — body should stay relaxed
notes: Work on this — you should be able to eventually get power on the shot even in this small surface area. Don't worry if it's lighter at first, keep working!

title: Catch & Release Shot
description: Game-like catch and release shot. Train receiving a pass and getting the shot off quickly with your head up — simulates in-game timing.
whatYouNeed: A passer (or a helper), a pile of pucks, a net
dos: Receive the puck and get the shot off quickly
Pick a spot, hit it a few times before switching targets
Keep your head up — scan the net before the shot comes off
Lefties: go low blocker. Righties: go low glove
Build the habit of seeing what the goalie is giving you
donts: Don't look down for a long time — eyes should be scanning the net before you release

title: High Slot One-Timer
description: High slot one-timer drill. Train reading the pass, picking your spot, and snapping it off quick from the slot — simulates the most dangerous scoring area on the ice.
whatYouNeed: A passer (or helper), a pile of pucks, a net
dos: Lefties: shoot top right (right side of net) — where the goalie is sliding toward
Righties: shoot top left (opposite corner)
On a slow pass, go across the grain
Hit five in one spot before moving to the next target
Snap it quick — high slot windows close fast
donts: Don't raise your stick above your head like a slap shot
This is a high slot one-timer, not a blue line bomb — keep the stick lower and snap through the puck
